_note: Hand-curated. Roll ids are chosen by reading the Clerk's titles; her vote is pulled from data/votes.json, never typed here. statementRx matches titles; statementPicks adds specific releases with a verbatim snippet found by 'rx' in the release's full text (data/statements_full.json). No editorial verdicts except the Israel card's headline, set in 'israel.headline'.

issues.name: Immigration and ICE
issues.intro: Votes on the Laken Riley Act, Homeland Security nominees and amendments on ICE funding and DACA, plus his statements on individual detention cases.

issues.name: Economy, housing and cost of living
issues.intro: The 2025 and 2026 reconciliation bills, tariffs, rescissions and funding bills, housing, and his Banking Committee work on lenders and markets.

issues.name: Public safety and the military at home
issues.intro: Police funding, fentanyl penalties, and limits on using the National Guard and the military in law enforcement, including his own amendment.

issues.name: Technology, AI and crypto
issues.intro: His calls for AI safety rules and his vote on the stablecoin bill.

issues.name: War powers and foreign policy
issues.intro: Votes to remove U.S. forces from hostilities not authorized by Congress (Iran, Venezuela), and his statement on the funding fight over the Iran war.

issues.name: Money in politics and democracy
issues.intro: His bill on political giving by federal contractors.

israel.question: Israel or Palestine?
israel.headline: Leans Palestine
israel.headlineWhy: The headline names the side that most items on this card point to, and says “leans” when some items point elsewhere. Here {npal} items point toward Palestine, {nisr} toward Israel and {nmixed} are mixed.
israel.summary: He voted for every resolution on this card that would block arms sales to Israel or require reports on its human rights record. He led the NDAA push to drop provisions on U.S.-Israel defense cooperation, and in statements he mourned the October 7 victims and called for accountability for violence in the West Bank.

items.text: Voted {vote} on both of Sen. Sanders's April 2025 resolutions to block arms sales to Israel. Both failed.
Voted {vote} on both July 2025 resolutions to block weapons sales and exports to Israel. Both failed.
Voted {vote} on both April 2026 resolutions to block arms sales to Israel. Both failed.
Voted {vote} to force a State Department report on Israel's human rights practices (S.Res. 852). It failed {yea}–{nay}; the Democratic caucus voted {cY}–{cN}.

items.rx: nine American citizens have been killed
items.text: After the vote on his privileged resolution on West Bank violence, said nine American citizens have been killed in recent years without accountability.
On the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, remembered the hundreds of lives lost and the hostages, and said civilians in Gaza bear a staggering daily toll.
